scenes.heading: Pathogens and disease
scenes.sub: What causes disease, and how does it spread?
scenes.say: A disease is any condition that stops part of your body working normally. Some are caused by tiny invaders. Knowing what causes a disease and how it spreads is the first step in stopping it.

scenes.heading: Two kinds of disease
scenes.say: Infectious diseases are caused by a pathogen and can be caught, like the flu or malaria. Non-infectious diseases can't be caught. They come from genes, lifestyle, the environment or diet, like cystic fibrosis or scurvy.

scenes.heading: Bad Viruses Find People Pleasant
points: Viruses: not cells; genes in a protein coat
Parasites: like tapeworms and head lice
scenes.say: There are five pathogen types: Bad Viruses Find People Pleasant. Bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa and parasites. Bacteria are prokaryotic cells with no nucleus. Most bacteria are actually harmless or helpful. Fungi and protozoa are eukaryotic. Viruses aren't cells at all.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Malware gets onto a phone and uses its processor to copy itself
scenes.science: A virus enters a host cell and uses its machinery to copy itself
scenes.breaks: malware is written on purpose; viruses are natural and have no goal. And cells destroyed by a virus are gone for good.
scenes.say: A virus is like malware on your phone. It can't do anything by itself. It gets into a host cell, hijacks the cell's machinery to make copies of itself, and the new viruses often burst out, destroying the cell.

scenes.heading: How pathogens spread
scenes.say: Pathogens spread by direct contact, by touching contaminated objects called fomites, through droplets from coughs and sneezes, in contaminated food and water, through body fluids, and by vectors.

scenes.heading: A vector is a delivery driver
scenes.everyday: A delivery rider carries food but doesn't eat it
scenes.science: A mosquito carries the malaria pathogen but doesn't get malaria
scenes.breaks: a driver carries a sealed bag, but in many vectors the pathogen lives and develops inside the vector first.
scenes.say: A vector is like a food delivery driver, not the customer. A mosquito picks up the malaria protozoan from one person and drops it into the next when it bites, without getting malaria itself.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: After a flood, many people in one area get diarrhoea. They share a water supply. Likely route, and one control?
lines: What do they share? The water supply
Floods can wash sewage into water
Control: boil or treat drinking water
scenes.say: After a flood, many people in one area get diarrhoea. What do they share? The same water supply, and floods can wash sewage into water. So the route is contaminated water. Boiling or treating drinking water breaks the chain.

points: Viruses only reproduce inside host cells
Hygiene breaks the chain of transmission
scenes.say: Quick recap. There are five pathogen types. Viruses can only reproduce inside host cells. Non-infectious diseases can't be caught. And handwashing, clean water and cooking food properly all break the chain of transmission. Now try the practice questions!
